text:
mike: Heads up — we're seeing a sustained p50/p95 jump for hosted inference in us-west-2 around ~03:00 UTC. Started ~03:01.

tara: Noticing throughput drop as well on several Dedicated pools, correlated with driver rollout logs? :thinking:

deploy-bot: deploy completed: driver-update/cuda-12.2.1 -> 12.2.3 on g4 clusters at 02:47 UTC

mike: That lines up. Latency graphs look like kernel fallbacks — a lot more small kernels running per token.

elaine: Can you paste profiler snippet? nvprof / Nsight stats would help.

mike: Sure — short excerpt from umbrella profile (truncated):
```
KernelName             Calls   Time(ms)    Avg(ms)
flash_attn_fwd         1200    3400         2.83
gemm_small             4300    11200        2.60
softmax_fallback       4100    9300         2.27
```
Looks like flash_attn calls dropped and softmax_fallback/gemm_small increased.

devin: We also saw an uptick in KV cache evictions on that pool — retention dropped ~30% after the driver update.

sam: Evictions would cause more KV recompute and smaller attention windows, increasing kernel churn.

mike: Paging eng-runtime — @narayan have we changed kernel selector thresholds recently? Could driver bump change heuristic results?

narayan: Not deployed any selector changes this week. But CUDA driver ABI changes can shift heuristics in Triton (kernel autotuner) — some heuristics use blockDim/warp occupancy and now reported occupancy numbers changed.

tara: I dug into the routing logs: requests with seq_len 128->256 are being routed to non-quantized model variant in a fallback path more often. That means different kernel set.

elaine: Reproduced locally with a small workload and CUDA 12.2.3 — flash_attn kernels fail to launch on certain SM configs and fall back to Triton generic kernels.

mike: Any stack traces or error codes? We need exact failure reason.

elaine: Error log from runtime:
```
E InferenceRuntime: kernel_launch failed: cudaErrorLaunchFailure (err=719)
E Kernel: flash_attn_fwd_sm80
E Falling back to: flash_attn_generic
```

devin: 719 is launch failure; could be due to increased register usage after driver internal changes leading to block size invalidation.

narayan: On a hunch I tested forcing flash_attn_generic -> flash_attn_fast via selector override and that restored p95 close to baseline.

sam: Good to know — can we make selector prefer the fast kernel for the problematic seq_len range as a temporary mitigation?

narayan: Yes, I can push a config override to Dedicated pools in us-west-2: selector.rule(seq_len in [64,256]) -> prefer flash_attn_fast. Will roll canary to 10%.

deploy-bot: config-update applied by narayan: kernel-selector override canary=10% at 04:12 UTC

mike: After canary: p95 dropped ~40% on canary nodes within 5 minutes. No regression observed.

tara: On the eviction side, increasing KV cache TTL for translated keys mitigates recompute pressure while we diagnose the driver/kernel mismatch.

devin: TTL bump proposal: keys TTL +120s for affected pools — low risk. Approving.

sam: Also adding a perf CI job to run kernel autotuner against latest CUDA driver matrix so we catch these shifts earlier.

narayan: I'll follow up with a repro job that runs Nsight and dumps kernel attributes (registers, shared mem) for both flash and fallback kernels under 12.2.3 vs 12.2.1.

elaine: Logged bug in internal tracker: PERF-1124 — flashattn kernel launch failures after cuda 12.2.3. Added profile artifacts and sample request.

mike: Summary of immediate actions: 1) selector override canary (done), 2) KV TTL bump (done), 3) perf CI autotuner added (in progress), 4) driver/Oem vendor confirm (open).

sam: Heads up to support — add note for customers on affected Dedicated pools; status page tick required if we see broader impact.

narayan: Will also add a temporary metric to show flash_attn_fwd call ratio to make regression alerts simpler.

mike: Thanks everyone. If we see reappearance after wider rollout we rollback driver or expand selector override. Keeping this thread for follow-ups. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: alert cleared for us-west-2 p95 spikes at 04:38 UTC. Monitoring for 2h

mike: last check — p95 stable and throughput recovered on canary; leaving monitoring on. Thanks all.
